A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. The added table and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of seven LVLMs on human referential dialogues, including accuracy results, robustness analyses, and follow-up experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally tabulates pairwise starting-round comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain the same transcript-and-image matching procedure, prompting, and experimental variants. Completing a sentence in Section 7 does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 80 dialogues from 10 human pairs, basket and dog images, four conversational rounds, and follow-up scenarios.

E2.justification: The seven evaluated LVLMs remain unchanged, as do the GPT-4o and Qwen-2.5-VL-32B follow-up comparisons. Added Table 9 uses the existing model set.

E3.justification: Starting rounds, image-order controls, accuracy measurement, and prompting settings are unchanged. Table 9 reports the single-start comparisons already described in v1, without establishing a new protocol or rerun.

E4.justification: Table 9 expands the evidence for the existing early-versus-late-start analysis with detailed pairwise single-round comparisons. The analytical question already appears in Section 6.2 and Appendix C.2 of v1; other robustness, follow-up, and error analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Repeated-run counts, confidence-interval reporting, paired t-tests, and significance conventions were already documented in v1. Table 9 adds significance outcomes using these practices, without documenting additional runs or a changed uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 9 supplies previously untabulated mean differences and significance markers across starting rounds, including GPT-4o's 14.0-percentage-point R1-minus-R3 difference for baskets, marked p < 0.01. Existing numerical results remain unchanged; Gemini-2.0-Flash's 7-point advantage for R2 over R1 was already stated in v1.

T1.justification: The theoretical background and definitions used for performance trends remain unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the corpus-release contribution and claims that LVLMs struggle with spontaneous referential communication and fail to improve consistently across rounds.

C2.justification: Interpretations of starting-round effects, model performance, and follow-up experiments are unchanged. Limitations concerning corpus size, missing human-overhearer baselines, variability, and model coverage are also retained.

D1.justification: Model versions, hardware, image-order generation, prompt templates, and code/corpus access information remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices B and D.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, bibliography, and positioning relative to psycholinguistic overhearing studies and visual-grounding research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 completes Section 7's unfinished sentence about how transcripts are parceled out. It also replaces Section 6.2's unresolved table reference and Appendix C.2's incorrect Table 2 reference with Table 9, and updates references following renumbering.

P2.justification: v2 inserts a full-page Table 9 showing single-start comparisons with significance highlighting. Former Tables 9 and 10 become Tables 10 and 11; subsequent appendix pages shift, while existing figures and table displays remain otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 fills the missing-table gap behind Section 6.2 and Appendix C.2, making the existing starting-round claims easier to inspect. Corrected references and the completed sentence improve readability. These are limited gains in completeness and clarity; the experimental design, central findings, and limitations remain unchanged.
